messages:
rachel (prod): Quick sync: major customer asked for day-0 legal-hold export capability. They want auditor-ready artifacts on day of onboarding. We need an MVP plan that doesn't block the launch.
lee (eng): Clarify scope: do they want continuous streaming of audit events or a one-time snapshot/export on demand?
cody (cs): Customer said: immediate snapshot at onboarding + ad-hoc legal-hold exports. Not continuous. Also they expect auth + request metadata + model invocation traces.
hangi (infra): Snapshot approach is doable. We can re-use current audit log pipeline to emit daily snapshots and add an on-demand export endpoint. Realtime stream would be a bigger infra lift.
tess (security): Requirements for SOC2/ISO: exported artifacts must be tamper-evident, include chain-of-custody metadata, and be reproducible for auditors (checksums, signer, timestamp). We should also support BYOK for encryption pre-handoff.
nina (legal): We'll need export contract terms that shift post-handoff custody to customer. Also require an approval/authorization audit trail for who requested the export. Add a minimum retention-we-offer clause (e.g., 30/90/365 tiers).
omar (sales): Pricing signal: customers expect this as enterprise feature. Recommend a paid add-on or included for pilot customers. Need concise collateral for Sales engineers.
rachel (prod): Proposal for MVP: 1) On-demand export API that packages tenant artifacts for selected time range 2) Signed manifest (HMAC) + sha256 checksums 3) Optional BYOK encrypt-to-customer-key if customer provides 4) Pilot with 2-3 customers, 90-day on-platform retention default.
lee (eng): Implementation bullets: - API: POST /v1/tenants/:id/exports {start,end,include_traces:true} - backend job that composes ZIP of logs + manifest.json - manifest fields: tenant_id, window, files[], checksums[], signed_by - verification job that validates checksums post-write.
hangi (infra): Storage options: A) write to customer-provided S3 (preferred, reduces our custody) B) write to Redwood staging bucket + short TTL and handoff. If we host, need ephemeral encryption keys and key-rotation doc. Also: support Parquet for large logs vs gz for small ones.
tess (security): MVP gating checklist: - manifest signature enabled (HMAC or KMS sign) - keystore fingerprint in manifest if BYOK used - export ACLs validated by policy - export request recorded in internal audit trail - playbook for failed verification/retry.
nina (legal): Add to ops checklist: require customer's POA (proof-of-authority) before releasing day-0 export. We should not auto-release without an approved contact.
omar (sales): Can we expose estimated GB & cost before export? Customers want cost predictability.
hangi (infra): We can run a dry-run estimate (calculate bytes based on retention window) and return a cost estimate in response. But accurate size needs sampling; add a warning.
codelate (typo) deploy-bot: export-pipeline job queued by @lee  ETA 1d for staging provisioning.
lee (eng): Effort estimate: MVP export endpoint + manifest signing + write-to-S3 = roughly 3 dev sprints (2 backend, 1 infra/ops). Verification + BYOK optional add ~1 sprint.
rachel (prod): Tradeoffs for prioritization: - Quick path: HMAC-signed manifests + customer S3 => minimal infra exposure (fastest) - Full path: BYOK + escrow + WORM storage => higher confidence for auditors but longer build.
tess (security): For long term we should aim for immutable object storage (WORM) + KMS integration where customer keys can perform envelope encryption and we keep signed attestations. That's needed for strict regulatory customers.
nina (legal): Contract language must: limit Redwood liability after handoff, require customer attestation of secure custody, specify notification timelines for verification failures, and list supported retention tiers. I'll draft a short addendum.
ar (cody): Pilot acceptance criteria suggested: 1) Successful export + manifest verification for 3 customers 2) Manual review of one restored archive by Security + Legal 3) SLA on export verification run (<1h for <100GB)
omar (sales): Add: playbook for rollback if export contains PII not expected. Customers ask for quick remediation steps.
lee (eng): Dev checklist: - Export job composer - manifest signer (HMAC service key) - API + RBAC enforcement - write-to-target (customer s3 or redwood staging) - post-write verification job - audit entry for who requested export - onboarding doc for infra team
tess (security): Require tests: integrity test, BYOK handshake test, permission audit test. Also ensure manifests include keystore thumbprint and operator id.
rachel (prod): Decision point: MVP scope locked to on-demand snapshot + HMAC manifests + customer S3 write. BYOK and staging-hosted exports are stretch. Agree?
hangi (infra): +1 for MVP. Minimizes our storage responsibilities.
nina (legal): Agree, with requirement that we capture POA prior to export.
omar (sales): Good for timeline. We'll position BYOK as premium.
cody (cs): I'll collect pilot customer contacts and consent templates.
lee (eng): I'll open RFC + spike for sampling/size estimation today. Will tag architecture for Parquet vs gz decisions.
rachel (prod): Timelines: RFC by EOD Tue, MVP alpha for pilot in 6 weeks. Legal addendum draft by Wed. Security checklist by Fri.
deploy-bot: reminder  create runbook /runbooks/export-handback and incident template /runbooks/export-verify-failure
rachel (prod): Thanks team. If you have objections to the MVP choice (HMAC + customer S3 only) call now or file in RFC. Closing thread.
